\section[el liderazgo]{el liderazgo — the leadership}

\label{lesson:ES-C594-liderazgo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to do for a living, then the Spanish for efficient.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el liderazgo}
\textbf{el liderazgo} — \textquotedblleft{}the leadership\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Necesitamos un buen liderazgo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We need good leadership.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{el líder} — the leader.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{liderazgo} is built on \emph{líder}, which was borrowed from English \emph{leader} (EtymDB), with the ending \emph{-azgo}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el liderazgo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el liderazgo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el liderazgo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to do for a living, then the Spanish for efficient, then say \emph{el liderazgo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el liderazgo mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The leadership\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[motivar]{motivar — to motivate}

\label{lesson:ES-C594-motivar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for efficient, then the Spanish for the leadership.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: motivar}
\textbf{motivar} — \textquotedblleft{}to motivate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Un buen jefe sabe motivar a la gente.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{A good boss knows how to motivate people.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Estar motivado} — to be motivated.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{motivar} is built on \emph{motivo}, a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{motivus} 'moving' (EtymDB), from \emph{movere} 'to move'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{motivar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{motivar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{motivar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for efficient, then the Spanish for the leadership, then say \emph{motivar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does motivar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To motivate\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la colaboración]{la colaboración — the collaboration, the help}

\label{lesson:ES-C594-colaboracion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the leadership, then the Spanish for to motivate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la colaboración}
\textbf{la colaboración} — \textquotedblleft{}the collaboration, the help\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Gracias por tu colaboración.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Thank you for your help.}
\end{quote}

A polite word on notices: \emph{agradecemos su colaboración}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{colaboración} is built on \emph{colaborar}, a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{collaborare}, from \emph{laborare} 'to work' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[dirigir]{dirigir — to run, to manage; to direct}

\label{lesson:ES-C594-dirigir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to motivate, then the Spanish for the collaboration.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: dirigir}
\textbf{dirigir} — \textquotedblleft{}to run, to manage; to direct\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ella dirige el proyecto.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She runs the project.}
\end{quote}

Spelling: \emph{dirijo}. \emph{Dirigir una película} — to direct a film.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dirigir} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{dirigere} 'to set straight, to direct', built on \emph{regere} 'to guide, to rule' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to motivate, then the Spanish for the collaboration, then say \emph{dirigir} again
\end{itemize}

\section[gestionar]{gestionar — to manage, to handle}

\label{lesson:ES-C594-gestionar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the collaboration, then the Spanish for to run.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: gestionar}
\textbf{gestionar} — \textquotedblleft{}to manage, to handle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Gestiono los pedidos de la tienda.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I manage the shop's orders.}
\end{quote}

For paperwork too: \emph{gestionar un permiso}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gestionar} is built on \emph{gestión}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{gestio} 'management', from \emph{gerere} 'to carry, to carry on' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
